title: Core E: Cellular and Organismic Systems for Antiviral Testing
text:
Core E – Cellular and Organismic Systems for Antiviral Testing
Relevance
Readily available and efficacious interventions for viruses with pandemic potential are desperately needed.
Antiviral testing using live virus in relevant cell and animal models is essential to evaluate drugs these drugs.
This Core’s expertise in coronaviruses, flaviviruses, arenaviruses and filoviruses will allow us to provide
rigorous antiviral evaluation in coordination with the 5 projects and 5 other cores.

title: Signature Project
text: Suicide is a leading cause of death among young adults (ages 18–34), representing a significant public health crisis. The Safety Planning Intervention (SPI) is an evidence-based, scalable suicide prevention tool; however, ensuring its continued use remains a challenge, particularly among young adults navigating the transition to adulthood. The Supporting Transitions to Adulthood to Reduce Suicide (STARS) program integrates SPI with digital peer mentorship to enhance safety plan quality and adherence. In preliminary work, STARS showed high engagement and acceptability, yet rigid protocols limited peer mentors’ ability to respond to participants’ evolving needs. Near real-time feedback—using digital assessments and artificial intelligence (AI)—offers a novel strategy to support responsive, patient-centered peer mentoring. This project will conduct a three-arm, Type 2 hybrid effectiveness-implementation randomized controlled trial to evaluate the comparative effectiveness of: (1) SPI alone (Control), (2) SPI with peer mentorship (STARS), and (3) SPI with peer mentorship enhanced by near real-time feedback (STARS+). We will enroll 600 young adults with recent suicidal ideation and assess outcomes over time. The primary clinical outcome is suicidal ideation; secondary outcomes include suicide attempts and mechanisms of change such as safety plan use. Implementation outcomes include fidelity, adoption, acceptability, feasibility, and cost. Specific Aims are: (1) Develop an implementation strategy to integrate near real-time client feedback into STARS using machine learning and human-centered design; (2) Evaluate the clinical effectiveness of SPI, STARS, and STARS+ on suicidal ideation and attempts; and (3) Assess implementation outcomes and cost of peer mentorship with and without near real-time feedback. This research is innovative in its integration of AI-powered feedback into suicide prevention and will provide critical evidence on how peer-delivered, data-informed interventions can enhance the personalization, quality, and reach of SPI. Findings will inform scalable, sustainable strategies to reduce suicide risk among young adults.

title: Improving Quality of End-of-Life Care for Veterans Receiving Hospice in Community Nursing Homes
text:
VA is a national leader in the provision of high-quality hospice and palliative care, particularly in
VA Community Living Centers (CLCs). Yet the demand for CLC-based hospice care has
outpaced supply, a gap that is expected to increase with the aging of the Veteran population. To
address this need, VA contracts with community nursing homes (CNHs) and hospice agencies
to provide CNH-based hospice care to Veterans. Our preliminary work has revealed that quality
ratings of EOL care provided in CNHs are soberingly lower than in VA CLCs. Thus, VA must
identify ways to improve quality of EOL care in CNHs. This novel project uses a mixed methods
design to develop a rich understanding of the structural characteristics and care processes that
are associated with the provision of high-quality CNH-based hospice care. The results will be
used to inform policies and practices that improve the quality of EOL care provided in CNHs.

title: Quantifying the Effects of Shear Flow on Blood using a Magnetically Levitated Device
text:
Blood pumps and other blood contacting medical devices may cause damage to the cells within
the blood itself. Pumps designers design these devices to minimize these negative effects, but
no reliable method is currently available to accurately predict these effects during the design
process. This project will utilize a novel device developed by our lab to improve our understanding
of the effects of shear flow on blood cell viability which will provide critical information to guide the
development of next generation blood pumps or other blood contacting medical devices.

title: Mechanisms of human papillomavirus entry
text: The human papillomaviruses (HPV) are responsible for approximately 5% of all cancers worldwide and most people will remain unvaccinated against HPV for the foreseeable future. We have identified and characterized cellular proteins required for HPV infection, and here we will focus on the role of these proteins in trafficking of HPV to the nucleus during infection. These studies will provide proof-of-principle of new approaches to inhibit infection by these important human tumor viruses and the cancers they cause and provide new insights into fundamental cellular processes.

title: Developing synthetic RNA organelles for spatiotemporal separation, control, and monitoring in living cells
text:
Artificial biomolecular condensates are emerging as a groundbreaking technology to manipulate
diverse cellular processes including gene regulation, metabolism, and stress. This project
establishes a new class of artificial condensates using computationally-designed RNA as a
building block. We will develop methods to customize RNA condensates to recruit a multitude of
target molecules and to form at target cellular locations, providing tools for control of gene
expression and biosensing that are immediately portable to a variety of organisms.

title: Cilia and Centrosomes
text:
Defects in cilia lead to developmental disorders and disease ranging from congenital heart defects, bone
malformations and inherited kidney disease to blindness, obesity and cancer. The goal of this proposal is to
support junior investigators to attend the 2026, 2028 and 2030 FASEB SRC on Cilia and Centrosomes. The
meeting will promote and advance research on cilia and cilia-related disease, facilitate collaborations between
basic and physician investigators, and provide training and career development for junior scientists.

title: Dissecting AAV silencing in humanized mice
text:
Transgene silencing has been identified as a clinical hurdle for long-term AAV gene therapy
approaches. We will dissect vector genome silencing mechanisms and explore potential therapeutic
strategies in a novel human liver chimeric mouse model using xenografted human hepatocytes from
patients with metabolic liver disease.

title: Elucidating and Directing Heteromolecular Mechanobiology with Nanoengineered Cell Interfaces
text:
Despite recent progresses in mechanobiology research, there is still a fundamental knowledge gap in critical
cellular functions and molecular mechanisms, which take place between the molecular and cellular scale.
Combining the state-of-the-art top-down nanotechnology and the bottom-up synthetic biology, we will create
artificial cell interfaces with multiplexed physicochemical features to elucidate and direct cellular functions.
Considering the interplay and crosstalk between multiple receptors and physicochemical cues, we will reveal the
underlying synergistic mechanisms of heteromolecular mechanobiology for cell-extracellular matrix signaling
(fibroblast as a model) and cell-cell signaling (T cell as a model).

title: Update of the WTC Cancer Tissue Biobank
text:
We address the increase cancer incidence among the World Trade Center (WTC) responders by updating the
WTC tissue bank system with the newly diagnosed cancers (after 2018), and to link the tissue bank with Biome
to access complete medical record history, and blood samples collected before or after a cancer diagnosis for
WTC cancers who are also MSSM patients.
PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE: The biobank will represent the necessary infrastructure for addressing
questions such as the link between specific carcinogens exposures and certain cancer sites, molecular
signatures of exposure that could be linked to cancer, specific markers of tumor aggressiveness among WTC
responders.

title: Advancing FTIR-based Multimodal Imaging with AI for Risk Stratification of Oral Precancer
text:
A significant portion of oral cancer is preceded by precancerous clinical lesions known as oral potentially
malignant disorders (OPMDs). The objective of this proposal is to develop and validate a multimodal imaging
diagnostic system that integrates Fourier transform infrared spectroscopic imaging with histological imaging,
enhanced by advanced machine learning and deep learning approaches. The proposed system will enable
objective, accurate, and personalized risk stratification for OPMDs, supporting clinicians in effective diagnosis
and management of oral precancer, facilitating early oral cancer detection and improving patient outcomes.

title: Risk stratification of malaria among school-age children with mHealth spectroscopy of blood analysis
text: Noninvasive detection of malaria strengthens biosecurity preparedness while supporting the development of low-cost mobile health technologies that can later be adapted for rural, community-based, and at-home health settings with limited access to diagnostic services. The proposed mHealth technology will help identify children who are most likely to need malaria testing and treatment, maximize available resources, and generate scalable strategies relevant to both settings with limited healthcare access and US public health preparedness.

title: Development of SUV39H1-selective inhibitor for human colon cancer therapy
text:
This proposal will develop the SUV39H1-selective small molecule inhibitor F5446 nanoparticle eNP-
F5446 to restore tumor cell sensitivity to cell death induction and to re-activate tumor-infiltrating CTL
effector function in colorectal cancer. eNP-F5446 is expected to overcome human colorectal cancer
resistance to PD-(L)1 blockade immunotherapy.

title: Investigating metformin and cocaine interactions in the brain at the level of pharmacokinetics, physiology, and proteomics
text:
Despite years of research into the neurobiological basis of cocaine use disorder (CUD), there remains no FDA-
approved pharmacological therapy. Our preclinical studies provide support for repurposing metformin, a drug
prescribed mainly for the treatment of type 2 diabetes, for the treatment of CUD. The primary objective of this
project is to carry out a systematic interrogation of the cellular and molecular mechanisms of metformin in the
brain that mediate the drug's effects on cocaine related behaviors utilizing integrative pharmacokinetic, molecular
biology, in vivo imaging, and proteomic techniques.

title: Advancing Protein Isoform Analysis through an Integrated Computational Framework.
text:
Alternative splicing, a process where genes create different versions of proteins, is crucial for normal
cell function. In cancer, this process often goes awry, leading to the production of harmful proteins that fuel
tumor growth and spread. Our project aims to develop novel informatics tools to comprehensively understand
these aberrant proteins, with the ultimate goal of facilitating the discovery of novel biomarkers and the
development of precisely targeted therapies for cancer patients.

title: Vascular regulation of fatty acid transport in metastatic tumor outgrowth
text:
Metastatic outgrowth of tumor cells requires nutrients to fuel cell proliferation. Blood
vessels play a critical role in supplying nutrients. This application investigates how
mTORC1, a signaling molecule, in regulating fatty acids transport across blood vessel
to support tumor metastasis.

title: Elucidating the molecular basis of piperaquine resistance in Plasmodium falciparum
text:
Piperaquine is a vital drug in the fight against malaria, yet resistance has emerged in Southeast Asia.
Our project will predict the risk that resistance emerges and spreads in Africa and will identify the causal
genetic factors in Plasmodium falciparum parasites. We will also define the molecular basis of
resistance and identify new chemical compounds that can suppress the resistance pathway in parasites.

title: Toxicant-induced neurotoxicity mediated by glia-neuron and gene-environment interactions in Parkinson's disease
text:
In the United States alone, about one million people have Parkinson’s disease and 50-60,000 new cases
of PD are diagnosed each year. The causes of PD in most of these cases remain unknown; however,
environmental factors have been implicated. The focus of this grant is of two folds: first, to elucidate the
mechanisms by which manganese induces neurotoxicity through impaired autophagy and second, to identify
potential novel therapeutic targets for PD.

title: p16 Cellular Senescence and Vascular Dysfunction in Sleep Apnea
text:
The physiological and molecular mechanisms of Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA)-induced vascular senescence
leading to vascular dysfunction remain to be elucidated. Transgenic mouse models enable the detection and
selective ablation of cells expressing p16, a known marker of cellular senescence. These models will be exposed
to Intermittent Hypoxia and Sleep Fragmentation to investigate aorta and coronary artery function, epigenetic
age acceleration and molecular alterations induced by OSA in cardiovascular dysfunction.

title: COBRE Phase III: Delaware Center for Neuroscience Research
text:
Delaware Center for Neuroscience Research
Public Health Relevance
Summary
The foundation of Phase III proposal is Delaware’s expanding set
of human and research resources in neuroscience, which has
Delaware neuroscience research competitive on a national level.
Our project supports research aimed at determining how thoughts, memories, feelings and
actions emerge from dynamic activities in the brain and are changed over time; as well
educational programs to develop a workforce that can participate in and benefit from
advances in our understanding of brain function. An increased understanding of how the
brain and nervous system functions will facilitate treatments for diseases and injuries and
provide insights into human behavior, biases, and cognition.
